'''Anthony Rex Hunter''' (born 23 August 1943) is a British-American biologist who is a professor of biology at the [[Salk Institute for Biological Studies]] and the [[University of California San Diego]]. His research publications list his name as Tony Hunter.<ref>{{Cite journal
| last1 = Bailis | first1 = J. M.
| last2 = Luche | first2 = D. D.
| last3 = Hunter | first3 = T.
| last4 = Forsburg | first4 = S. L.
| title = Minichromosome Maintenance Proteins Interact with Checkpoint and Recombination Proteins to Promote S-Phase Genome Stability
| doi = 10.1128/MCB.01717-07
| journal = Molecular and Cellular Biology
| volume = 28
| issue = 5
| pages = 1724–1738
| year = 2008
| pmid = 18180284
| pmc =2258774
}}</ref>

Professor Hunter is an elected member of the UK's [[Royal Society]] and the USA's [[National Academy of Sciences]].

==Early life and education==
Hunter was born in 1943 in the United Kingdom and educated at [[Felsted School]], prior to [[Christ's College, Cambridge]], where he was awarded a [[PhD]] in 1969 for research on [[protein synthesis]].<ref>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|title=Aspects of mammalian protein synthesis|first= Anthony Rex|last=Hunter|date=1969|url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.460063|oclc=500479081}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Following his PhD, Hunter held a fellowship at [[Christ's College, Cambridge]], in Cambridge (1968–1971) and (1973–1975). From 1971 to 1973, he was a [[postdoctoral research]] associate of the [[Salk Institute for Biological Studies]] in La Jolla, California. He was then assistant professor 1975–78, associate professor 1978–82, professor 1982 onwards and since 2008 director of the Salk Institute Cancer Center.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/h/7068/Anthony%20Rex%20%28Tony%29+HUNTER.aspx|title = Tony Hunter FRS|publisher = Debretts|access-date=18 July 2010}}</ref> He also sits on the Selection Committee for Life Science and Medicine which chooses winners of the [[Shaw Prize]].

Hunter is one of the foremost recognized leaders in the field of cell growth control, growth factor receptors and their signal transduction pathways. He is well known for discovering that tyrosine phosphorylation is a fundamental mechanism for transmembrane-signal transduction in response to growth factor stimulation and that disregulation of such tyrosine phosphorylation, by activated oncogenic protein [[tyrosine kinases]],<ref name=kingkinase>{{cite journal|last=Hunter|first=Tony|date=May 2008|title=Tony Hunter: kinase king. Interview by Ruth Williams|journal=[[J. Cell Biol.]]|volume=181|issue=4|pages=572–3| pmid = 18490508|doi = 10.1083/jcb.1814pi|pmc=2386096 }}</ref> is a pivotal mechanism utilized in the malignant transformation of cells. His work is important in signaling pathways and their disorders.

Hunter was a founder of Signal Pharmaceuticals.{{citation needed|date=May 2016}}

==Awards and honors==
He won the [[Wolf Prize in Medicine]] in 2005 for "the discovery of protein kinases that phosphorylate tyrosine residues in proteins, critical for the regulation of a wide variety of cellular events, including malignant transformation".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wolffund.org.il/cat.asp?id=24&cat_title=MEDICINE |title=The Wolf Prize in Medicine |access-date=2010-04-29 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090226015735/http://www.wolffund.org.il/cat.asp?id=24&cat_title=MEDICINE |archive-date=26 February 2009 }}. wolffund.org.il</ref> He has been granted along with [[Charles Sawyers]] and [[Joseph Schlessinger]] with the 2014 [[BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award]] in the Biomedicine category for "carving out the path that led to the development of a new class of successful cancer drugs".

* [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1987|1987 Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://royalsociety.org/Lists-of-Royal-Society-Fellows-1660-2007/ |title=Lists of Royal Society Fellows 1660–2007 |publisher=[[Royal Society]] |location=London |access-date=2010-07-18 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100324095152/http://royalsociety.org/Lists-of-Royal-Society-Fellows-1660-2007/ |archive-date=24 March 2010 }}</ref>
